segments.title: Neglect of Responsible Innovation
segments.quote: I'm not saying nobody believes it, I'm saying the reason it's in the document is the eight percent.
segments.full_text: Interviewer: The bid documents mention responsible innovation. How did that shape the work? Respondent: I'll be straight with you because I don't think there's much point otherwise. That language is in the bid because the evaluation matrix had a section for it worth eight percent. We wrote what scored well. I'm not saying nobody believes it, I'm saying the reason it's in the document is the eight percent. Interviewer: Was there anything behind the language? Respondent: There was a stakeholder engagement plan. It was two pages. It committed us to a launch event and a feedback email address. Both happened. The email address got nine messages in eighteen months, seven of them about a pothole.

codes.rationale: The engagement plan was superficial and not reviewed, indicating a lack of genuine public engagement.
The respondent dismisses the importance of responsible innovation, showing a lack of epistemic humility.

segments.title: Contractual Obligations
segments.quote: There was no review point in the contract. Contracts have review points for things somebody intends to check.

segments.title: Lack of Real Change
segments.quote: That would be a real filter. I couldn't produce them. Neither could my competitors. That would be a real filter.
segments.full_text: Interviewer: Do you think the project should have been done differently? Respondent: Differently, probably. Would a different consortium have done it better? I doubt it. Everybody bidding on municipal AI work is structured the same way, with the same incentives, answering the same matrix. codes.rationale: The respondent suggests that evidence of engagement is more important than intentions, indicating a lack of epistemic humility.
The respondent admits that no engagement plans have changed design decisions, indicating a lack of responsiveness.

summary: The respondent strongly exhibits a negative approach to responsible innovation, particularly in terms of engagement and reflexivity. The engagement plan was superficial and not reviewed, and the respondent dismisses the importance of responsible innovation. The lack of substantive changes in the project, despite the presence of an engagement plan, further highlights a lack of responsiveness. The respondent's suggestion that evidence of engagement is more important than intentions indicates a lack of epistemic humility.
transcript:
Interview transcript P06 — Business development lead, consortium partner
Case: Port Calder adaptive traffic signal and pedestrian detection system  |  SYNTHETIC DATA — not a real interview
[Interviewer] The bid documents mention responsible innovation. How did that shape the work?
[Respondent] I'll be straight with you because I don't think there's much point otherwise. That language is in the bid because the evaluation matrix had a section for it worth eight percent. We wrote what scored well. I'm not saying nobody believes it, I'm saying the reason it's in the document is the eight percent.
[Interviewer] Was there anything behind the language?
[Respondent] There was a stakeholder engagement plan. It was two pages. It committed us to a launch event and a feedback email address. Both happened. The email address got nine messages in eighteen months, seven of them about a pothole.
[Interviewer] Did anyone review whether the plan was working?
[Respondent] No. There was no review point in the contract. Contracts have review points for things somebody intends to check.
[Interviewer] Do you think the project should have been done differently?
[Respondent] Differently, probably. Would a different consortium have done it better? I doubt it. Everybody bidding on municipal AI work is structured the same way, with the same incentives, answering the same matrix. If you want a different outcome you have to change the matrix, not lecture the bidders.
[Interviewer] What would a better matrix ask for?
[Respondent] Evidence, not intentions. Don't ask me what my engagement plan is, ask me for the minutes of the last three times a plan like this changed a design decision. I couldn't produce them. Neither could my competitors. That would be a real filter.
